name: Creatine
short: Creatine is associated with a small rise in blood creatinine, described as transient, without a significant change in kidney filtration; no serious adverse outcomes in studies of women.
text: A 2025 meta-analysis found that creatine is associated with a modest rise in serum creatinine, which the authors describe as transient, which the authors attributed to metabolic turnover rather than kidney impairment, with no significant change in glomerular filtration rate. In a meta-analysis of studies in women (29 studies, 951 participants), no deaths or serious adverse outcomes were reported, and total adverse events, weight gain and measures of kidney and liver function did not differ significantly from comparison groups. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.

quotes: Creatine supplementation is associated with a modest, transient increase in serum creatinine levels, likely due to metabolic turnover rather than renal impairment.
No significant changes were observed in GFR, suggesting preserved kidney function.
citations.label: Naeini et al., 2025, BMC Nephrol
citations.title: Effect of creatine supplementation on kidney function: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

quotes: Twenty-nine studies monitored for adverse outcomes, with 951 participants.
There were no deaths or serious adverse outcomes reported.
No statistically significant difference was reported in measures of renal or hepatic function.
Nor does the use of creatine supplementation increase the risk of total adverse outcomes, weight gain or renal and hepatic complications in females.
citations.label: de Guingand et al., 2020, Nutrients
citations.title: Risk of Adverse Outcomes in Females Taking Oral Creatine Monohydrate: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
